Problem Domain:
Natural Language Processing (NLP), Text Mining, Data Engineering, Machine Learning Pipelines, Large-Scale Data Processing.

Project Description:
This project designs and implements a robust, scalable pipeline for preprocessing massive text datasets (potentially terabytes) in preparation for downstream document classification tasks. The pipeline leverages Pandas for efficient handling of metadata and text chunks, advanced regular expressions (Regex) for complex pattern matching, cleaning (e.g., removing HTML, special characters, PII), and rule-based feature extraction, and integrates Hugging Face Transformers for state-of-the-art tokenization aligned with pre-trained models (like BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT). The focus is on creating a modular, configurable, and potentially distributable pipeline (conceptually using Dask or Spark) that can handle diverse text formats, perform extensive cleaning and normalization, and generate features suitable for various document classification models. It emphasizes efficiency, reproducibility, and the ability to process data volumes beyond single-machine memory capacity.

Frameworks Used:

  • Core Data: Pandas, NumPy
  • NLP & Tokenization: Hugging Face transformers (for tokenizers), tokenizers (underlying library)
  • Text Cleaning: regex (advanced regular expressions), potentially BeautifulSoup4 (for HTML parsing), nltk (optional, for basic cleaning like stopword removal if needed before certain steps, though often handled by tokenizers).
  • Large-Scale Processing (Conceptual/Integration): Dask (for parallelizing Pandas operations), Apache Spark (via PySpark, for distributed processing).
  • Configuration: YAML
  • Workflow Orchestration (Conceptual): Airflow, Prefect, Dagster (for managing multi-step pipelines).
  • Storage: Efficient file formats (Parquet, Arrow) for intermediate and final data.

Dataset:
Processing massive text datasets requires access to large corpora. Examples:

  • Wikipedia Dumps: Full text dumps of Wikipedia articles (available in XML or other formats).
  • Common Crawl: Petabytes of web crawl data (requires significant filtering and processing).
  • PubMed Central Open Access Subset: Large collection of biomedical research articles.
  • News Corpora: Large datasets like AG News, Reuters Corpus, or custom collections from news APIs/archives.
  • Amazon Reviews / Yelp Reviews: Large collections of user-generated text.

For demonstration, we can use a moderately large, publicly available dataset like the AG News dataset or fetch a subset of Wikipedia articles.

Use Cases:

  1. Preparing Data for Text Classification: Generate clean, tokenized input suitable for training models to classify documents by topic, sentiment, intent, etc.
  2. Feature Extraction for ML: Create numerical representations (e.g., TF-IDF on cleaned tokens, embeddings from Transformers) from text for use in traditional ML models.
  3. Text Normalization: Standardize text data from diverse sources by removing noise, handling special characters, expanding contractions, etc.
  4. Corpus Cleaning: Apply the pipeline to large raw text corpora (like web crawls) to create cleaner versions for language modeling or other NLP research.
  5. Information Extraction Preprocessing: Clean and structure text before applying named entity recognition (NER), relation extraction, or other information extraction tasks.
  6. Compliance & Redaction: Use Regex components to identify and potentially mask or remove sensitive information (PII) at scale (requires careful pattern design and validation).

Full Development Lifecycle (Corporate View):

  1. Requirements & Data Source Identification (3-4 weeks): Define the downstream task (e.g., classification model requirements), identify the target text corpus/data sources, specify required cleaning steps (HTML removal, PII masking, normalization rules), choose the target Transformer model (influences tokenizer choice), and define performance metrics (processing throughput, data quality).
  2. Data Ingestion & Initial Exploration (4-6 weeks): Develop pipelines to ingest data from various sources (filesystems, databases, APIs). Perform initial EDA on a sample to understand text characteristics, encoding issues, noise patterns, and document structure. Set up storage for raw and processed data (e.g., data lake).
  3. Cleaning & Normalization Strategy Design (5-8 weeks): Define specific cleaning rules using Regex and potentially other libraries (BeautifulSoup). Develop strategies for handling case, punctuation, numbers, special characters, and encoding issues. Design rules for normalization (e.g., expanding contractions, standardizing date formats).
  4. Tokenizer Selection & Integration (2-3 weeks): Choose the appropriate Hugging Face tokenizer corresponding to the intended downstream model (e.g., BertTokenizerFast, RobertaTokenizerFast). Integrate the tokenizer into the pipeline.
  5. Pipeline Implementation (Modular) (8-12 weeks): Build the preprocessing pipeline as a series of modular steps (e.g., load -> clean_html -> normalize_text -> apply_regex -> tokenize). Use Pandas for efficient batch processing. Design for configuration using YAML.
  6. Scalability Integration (Conceptual/Implementation) (6-10 weeks): Adapt the Pandas-based pipeline to run in parallel using Dask or rewrite key components using PySpark for distributed processing on a cluster (e.g., Databricks, AWS EMR). Optimize data shuffling and serialization.
  7. Testing & Quality Assurance (4-6 weeks): Develop unit tests for individual cleaning/regex functions and integration tests for the full pipeline. Process a large sample and manually inspect the output quality. Measure processing time and resource usage.
  8. Deployment & Orchestration (4-6 weeks): Package the pipeline (e.g., Docker container). Deploy it to the target environment (cloud, on-premise cluster). Set up workflow orchestration (Airflow, Prefect) to run the pipeline on schedule or trigger-based.
  9. Monitoring & Maintenance (Ongoing): Monitor pipeline execution, data quality, and resource consumption. Update cleaning rules, regex patterns, and tokenizer versions as needed. Adapt to changes in input data characteristics.

# --- Filename: massive_nlp_preprocessing_pipeline.py ---

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import logging
import warnings
import time
import os
import yaml
import regex as re # Use the enhanced regex library
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional, Any, Callable

# NLP
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, PreTrainedTokenizerFast
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup # Optional: for HTML

# Parallel Processing (Conceptual Example with Dask)
import dask.dataframe as dd
from dask.diagnostics import ProgressBar

# Configuration
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(module)s - %(message)s")
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# --- Default Configuration ---
DEFAULT_CONFIG = {
    "text_column": "text",
    "tokenizer_name": "distilbert-base-uncased",
    "max_sequence_length": 512,
    "preprocessing_steps": [
        {"function": "remove_html", "enabled": True},
        {"function": "normalize_whitespace", "enabled": True},
        {"function": "lowercase", "enabled": True},
        # Add more steps: remove_urls, remove_emails, expand_contractions, remove_special_chars
        {"function": "remove_punctuation", "enabled": False, "keep": ".?!"}, # Example: keep some punctuation
        {"function": "tokenize", "enabled": True}
    ],
    "regex_features": [
        # Example: Count number of questions
        # {"name": "question_count", "pattern": r"\?+", "operation": "count"}
    ],
    "output_format": "parquet",
    "use_dask": False # Set to True to attempt Dask execution
}

# --- Preprocessing Functions ---
# Each function should accept text (str) and return processed text (str)

def remove_html(text: str) -> str:
    if not text or pd.isna(text):
        return ""
    try:
        # Use BeautifulSoup for robust HTML parsing
        soup = BeautifulSoup(text, "html.parser")
        return soup.get_text(separator=" ", strip=True)
    except Exception:
        # Fallback or basic regex if BS4 fails or is not installed
        return re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", text)

def normalize_whitespace(text: str) -> str:
    if not text or pd.isna(text):
        return ""
    # Replace multiple whitespace chars with a single space, strip leading/trailing
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()

def lowercase(text: str) -> str:
    if not text or pd.isna(text):
        return ""
    return text.lower()

def remove_punctuation(text: str, keep: str = "") -> str:
    if not text or pd.isna(text):
        return ""
    # Remove punctuation except characters in `keep`
    # \p{P} matches any punctuation character
    keep_pattern = f"[{re.escape(keep)}]" if keep else "" 
    pattern = r"[\p{P}" + (f"^" if keep else "") + keep_pattern + r"]+"
    try:
         return re.sub(pattern, " ", text) # Replace with space to avoid merging words
    except Exception as e:
         logging.warning(f"Regex failed for punctuation removal on text snippet: {text[:50]}... Error: {e}")
         return text # Return original on error

# --- Regex Feature Extractor ---
def extract_regex_features(text: str, features_config: List[Dict]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if not text or pd.isna(text):
        return {f[    name    ]: 0 for f in features_config} # Return default values

    results = {}
    for feature in features_config:
        name = feature[    name    ]
        pattern = feature[    pattern ]
        operation = feature.get(    operation   ,   count   ) # Default to count
        try:
            matches = re.findall(pattern, text)
            if operation ==     count   :
                results[name] = len(matches)
            elif operation ==     exists  :
                results[name] = 1 if matches else 0
            # Add more operations: sum_matched_numbers, extract_first, etc.
            else:
                 results[name] = 0 # Default for unknown operation
        except Exception as e:
            logging.warning(f"Regex feature     {name}   failed: {e}")
            results[name] = 0 # Default on error
    return results

# --- Tokenizer Function --- 
def tokenize_batch(texts: List[str], tokenizer: PreTrainedTokenizerFast, max_length: int) -> Dict[str, List]:
    if not texts:
        return {"input_ids": [], "attention_mask": []}
    # Handle potential None/NaN values in the batch before tokenizing
    cleaned_texts = [str(t) if pd.notna(t) else "" for t in texts]
    try:
        tokenized_output = tokenizer(
            cleaned_texts,
            add_special_tokens=True,
            max_length=max_length,
            padding="max_length", # Pad to max_length
            truncation=True,
            return_attention_mask=True,
            return_tensors=None # Return lists for easier DataFrame integration
        )
        return {
            "input_ids": tokenized_output["input_ids"],
            "attention_mask": tokenized_output["attention_mask"]
        }
    except Exception as e:
         logging.error(f"Tokenization failed: {e}. Returning empty lists.")
         # Return lists of correct shape but potentially empty/default values
         num_texts = len(texts)
         return {
             "input_ids": [[] for _ in range(num_texts)],
             "attention_mask": [[] for _ in range(num_texts)]
         }

# --- Pipeline Class ---
class NLPPreprocessor:
    def __init__(self, config: Dict):
        self.config = config
        self.text_column = config[    text_column ]
        self.tokenizer_name = config[    tokenizer_name  ]
        self.max_length = config[    max_sequence_length ]
        self.use_dask = config.get(    use_dask    , False)

        logging.info(f"Loading tokenizer: {self.tokenizer_name}")
        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(self.tokenizer_name, use_fast=True)
        logging.info("Tokenizer loaded.")

        # Map function names to actual functions
        self.step_functions: Dict[str, Callable] = {
            "remove_html": remove_html,
            "normalize_whitespace": normalize_whitespace,
            "lowercase": lowercase,
            "remove_punctuation": remove_punctuation,
            # Add other functions here
        }

    def _apply_steps(self, series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
        """Applies configured cleaning/normalization steps sequentially."""
        processed_series = series
        for step in self.config[    preprocessing_steps ]:
            func_name = step[    function    ]
            enabled = step.get(    enabled , True)

            if not enabled or func_name ==     tokenize    : # Tokenize is handled separately
                continue

            if func_name in self.step_functions:
                logging.info(f"Applying step: {func_name}")
                func = self.step_functions[func_name]
                # Get step-specific arguments (like `keep` for remove_punctuation)
                args = {k: v for k, v in step.items() if k not in ["function", "enabled"]}
                # Apply function element-wise
                processed_series = processed_series.apply(lambda x: func(x, **args) if pd.notna(x) else "")
            else:
                logging.warning(f"Preprocessing function     {func_name}  not found. Skipping.")
        return processed_series

    def process_dataframe(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Processes a Pandas DataFrame through the full pipeline."""
        logging.info(f"Starting preprocessing for DataFrame with shape {df.shape}")
        df_processed = df.copy()

        # 1. Apply cleaning/normalization steps
        cleaned_col_name = f"cleaned_{self.text_column}"
        df_processed[cleaned_col_name] = self._apply_steps(df_processed[self.text_column])

        # 2. Extract Regex Features (optional)
        if self.config.get(    regex_features  ):
            logging.info("Extracting regex features...")
            regex_results = df_processed[cleaned_col_name].apply(
                lambda x: extract_regex_features(x, self.config[    regex_features  ])
            )
            # Expand the dictionary results into columns
            regex_df = pd.json_normalize(regex_results)
            df_processed = pd.concat([df_processed, regex_df], axis=1)
            logging.info(f"Added regex features: {list(regex_df.columns)}")

        # 3. Tokenize
        tokenize_step = next((s for s in self.config[    preprocessing_steps ] if s[ function    ] ==    tokenize    ), None)
        if tokenize_step and tokenize_step.get(    enabled , True):
            logging.info("Tokenizing text...")
            # Process in batches for efficiency (though apply handles this reasonably)
            # For very large data, explicit batching or Dask map_partitions is better
            tokenized_output = tokenize_batch(df_processed[cleaned_col_name].tolist(), self.tokenizer, self.max_length)
            df_processed[    input_ids   ] = tokenized_output["input_ids"]
            df_processed[    attention_mask  ] = tokenized_output["attention_mask"]
            logging.info("Tokenization complete.")

        # Select and reorder columns for output
        output_columns = list(df.columns) + [cleaned_col_name]
        if self.config.get(    regex_features  ):
             output_columns.extend(regex_df.columns)
        if tokenize_step and tokenize_step.get(    enabled , True):
             output_columns.extend(["input_ids", "attention_mask"])
        # Ensure no duplicates and keep original order where possible
        final_columns = []
        for col in output_columns:
             if col not in final_columns:
                  final_columns.append(col)

        return df_processed[final_columns]

    def process_dask_dataframe(self, ddf: dd.DataFrame) -> dd.DataFrame:
        """Processes a Dask DataFrame (conceptual)."""
        logging.info(f"Starting preprocessing for Dask DataFrame with {ddf.npartitions} partitions")
        # Need to define meta for the output structure
        # This requires knowing the exact columns and dtypes produced
        # meta = ... (define expected output structure and dtypes)

        # 1. Apply cleaning/normalization via map_partitions
        cleaned_col_name = f"cleaned_{self.text_column}"
        # Need a wrapper function to apply steps to a partition (Pandas DataFrame)
        def apply_steps_partition(partition):
             return self._apply_steps(partition[self.text_column])
        # Define meta for the cleaned column
        meta_cleaned = pd.Series(dtype=str, name=cleaned_col_name)
        ddf[cleaned_col_name] = ddf.map_partitions(apply_steps_partition, meta=meta_cleaned)

        # 2. Extract Regex Features via map_partitions
        regex_feature_names = [f[    name    ] for f in self.config.get( regex_features  , [])]
        if regex_feature_names:
             logging.info("Extracting regex features with Dask...")
             def apply_regex_partition(partition):
                 results = partition[cleaned_col_name].apply(
                     lambda x: extract_regex_features(x, self.config[    regex_features  ])
                 )
                 return pd.json_normalize(results)
             # Define meta for regex features (assuming int counts)
             meta_regex = pd.DataFrame({name: pd.Series(dtype=int) for name in regex_feature_names})
             regex_ddf = ddf.map_partitions(apply_regex_partition, meta=meta_regex)
             # Align partitions might be needed before merging
             ddf = dd.concat([ddf, regex_ddf], axis=1)

        # 3. Tokenize via map_partitions
        tokenize_step = next((s for s in self.config[    preprocessing_steps ] if s[ function    ] ==    tokenize    ), None)
        if tokenize_step and tokenize_step.get(    enabled , True):
             logging.info("Tokenizing text with Dask...")
             def tokenize_partition(partition):
                 tokenized = tokenize_batch(partition[cleaned_col_name].tolist(), self.tokenizer, self.max_length)
                 # Return as DataFrame columns
                 return pd.DataFrame(tokenized, index=partition.index)
             # Define meta for tokenized output (list of ints)
             meta_tokenized = pd.DataFrame({
                 "input_ids": pd.Series(dtype=object), 
                 "attention_mask": pd.Series(dtype=object)
             })
             tokenized_ddf = ddf.map_partitions(tokenize_partition, meta=meta_tokenized)
             ddf = dd.concat([ddf, tokenized_ddf], axis=1)

        logging.info("Dask processing graph defined.")
        # Note: Computation happens only when `compute()` is called or data is saved.
        return ddf

# --- Main Execution Logic ---
if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.info("--- Starting NLP Preprocessing Pipeline --- ")

    # Load configuration
    config_path = "config_nlp.yaml"
    if os.path.exists(config_path):
        with open(config_path,     r   ) as f:
            config = yaml.safe_load(f)

    else:
        config = DEFAULT_CONFIG
        logging.warning(f"Config file {config_path} not found. Using default configuration.")

    # Load data (using AG News example)
    if ag_news_data is None:
        logging.error("Input data not loaded. Exiting.")
        exit()
    input_df = ag_news_data[    train   ] # Use training set for example
    logging.info(f"Input data shape: {input_df.shape}")

    # Instantiate preprocessor
    preprocessor = NLPPreprocessor(config)

    # Process data (Pandas or Dask)
    start_time = time.time()
    if config.get(    use_dask    , False):
        logging.info("Processing with Dask...")
        # Convert Pandas df to Dask df (adjust npartitions based on data size/cores)
        input_ddf = dd.from_pandas(input_df, npartitions=4)
        processed_ddf = preprocessor.process_dask_dataframe(input_ddf)

        # Trigger computation (e.g., by saving)
        output_path = "./output/processed_data_dask"
        logging.info(f"Saving processed Dask DataFrame to {output_path} (format: {config[    output_format   ]})...")
        os.makedirs(output_path, exist_ok=True)
        with ProgressBar():
            if config[    output_format   ] == "parquet":
                processed_ddf.to_parquet(output_path, engine=    pyarrow , write_index=False)
            elif config[    output_format   ] == "csv":
                 # CSV saving with Dask needs care with lists in columns
                 processed_ddf.to_csv(output_path, index=False, single_file=False) # Save as multiple files
            else:
                 logging.error(f"Unsupported Dask output format: {config[    output_format   ]}")
        # Load back a sample to show result (optional)
        # processed_df_sample = dd.read_parquet(output_path).head()

    else:
        logging.info("Processing with Pandas...")
        processed_df = preprocessor.process_dataframe(input_df)

        # Save processed data
        output_dir = "./output"
        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
        output_filename = f"processed_data_pandas.{config[    output_format   ]}"
        output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, output_filename)
        logging.info(f"Saving processed Pandas DataFrame to {output_path}...")
        if config[    output_format   ] == "parquet":
            processed_df.to_parquet(output_path, engine=    pyarrow , index=False)
        elif config[    output_format   ] == "csv":
             # Convert list columns to string for CSV compatibility
             list_cols = ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]
             for col in list_cols:
                 if col in processed_df.columns:
                      processed_df[col] = processed_df[col].apply(lambda x: json.dumps(x) if isinstance(x, list) else x)
             processed_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
        else:
             logging.error(f"Unsupported Pandas output format: {config[    output_format   ]}")

        print("\nSample Processed Data (Pandas):")
        print(processed_df.head())

    end_time = time.time()
